speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: One hand each, until you are tired of hands. The Cross is not the yard.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: I am not tired. I am considering it.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: He is considering it so he can drop the hand and call it judgment. I am keeping mine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: School broke at eleven. The market gets the rest of you, and it gets the hands first.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Butter. I can smell the stall from here. That is a fact about butter, not a request.

speaker: (the butter-woman)
text: Fourpence. It was threepence at Michaelmas, and I have said so to every basket since the frost.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fourpence, then. I am not arguing the year.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Fourpence is the price. Pay it, and do not make a speech of a firkin.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Threepence was before. Fourpence is the coin in the hand. I can hold both and still hold him.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: I am tired of hands.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then run ahead, and stop before the glove stall. Thy uncle is behind it.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: He has nodded. A nod is not a conversation, and I am not owed one. He is selling.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: I was not going to make him stop. I am running, which is the instruction.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Loving countryman! London agrees with you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Master Quiney. You have my hand, both of yours on it. I am well enough.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: I ask nothing of you. I ask it warmly. The town is glad of a face, and I will not put a purse in the sentence.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Leave that sentence standing. It is a good size.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Loving countryman. I have it in his voice, and he is not yet ten yards off.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Do not laugh, Hamnet.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: I am laughing. You told me not to, and I am.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: It sits in the mouth like a glove too fine for a Thursday. I am not apologising for the voice.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Let her keep it. A voice is not a theft. You look fed, Will. That is the whole of my inspection.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fed, and not questioned. I will take the warmth and leave the rest.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: They are ahead of us. Butter is fourpence. We are not a reception in the street.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: One laugh. I can stop at one. That is the bargain.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: I have the laugh counted. One. He will pretend the count is the stopping.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: One is a fair price. On you go, loving countryman. I have my own stall to be late for.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: On we go. Judith, the voice was for the Cross.
